info.title: vertice-bff
info.description:
The REST API the Vertice web and mobile apps call; it bridges HTTP/JSON to vertice-api over gRPC.

Every error is `{ error: { code, message, details? } }`: key on `code`, never on `message`. Besides the errors listed per operation, any call can answer 429 (global rate limit), 502 `UPSTREAM_ERROR` or 503 `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` (vertice-api refused or is down). Rules that do not fit a schema (ownership, rate limits, the time-zone rule) are in docs/api-contract.md.

get.description: Public: no token needed.

post.description: Public: no token needed. The password is checked by vertice-api. A wrong password, an unknown email and an account with no password yet all get the same 401 `UNAUTHORIZED` “Invalid email or password”. Failed attempts are rate limited. With `X-Vertice-Client: mobile` a TRAINER or CLIENT gets a 90-day mobile session, renewable with `POST /auth/session/renew`; without it the 8h web session. With the right password, a suspended account is 403 `ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED` (message: the text to show, “Sua conta está suspensa. Entre em contato com o suporte.”), and an ADMIN is 403 `ADMIN_LOGIN_ELSEWHERE` (message: “O acesso de alunos é feito somente pelo aplicativo Vertice.”), whatever `X-Vertice-Client` says: an admin signs in at `POST /admin/auth/login`. Neither gets a token.

post.description: Roles: TRAINER, CLIENT. Trades the caller’s mobile session token (from login or register with `X-Vertice-Client: mobile`) for a new one that expires 90 days from now; the old token stays valid until its own expiry. A web (8h) token is 403 `SESSION_NOT_RENEWABLE`, with or without the header: renewal decides from the token alone. vertice-api is asked first, so a token it no longer accepts (deleted user, changed role, password changed since the token was issued) is 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` and gets no new token. Refusals are rate limited per IP and per user. No body.
